newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares edge up on speculative demand.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares edge up on speculative demand.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index closed slightly higher on Monday, driven in part by speculative buying, brokers said.
The B share index edged up 0.48 point, or 0.53 percent, to close at 90.72 on turnover of HK$12.55 million, compared with HK$11.90 million on Friday.

Brokers said most institutional investors adopted a wait-and-see attitude towards trading on the eve of Hainan Dadonghai Tourism Centre (Holdings) Co Ltd's listing of 80 million class B shares on Tuesday.
Lizhu Pharmaceutical, which fell sharply on Friday, rallied HK$0.34, or 13.03 percent, to HK$2.95 on thin trade of 3,000 shares Monday.
Brokers said Shenzhen-based property concern China Vanke became Monday's second-best performer fueled by speculative buying, rising HK$0.23, or 5.79 percent, to HK$4.20 on volume of 36,000 shares.
China Bicycle followed, putting on HK$0.07, or 3.66 percent, to HK$1.98 and Tellus gained HK$0.06, or 3.57 percent, to HK$1.74. Jiangling Motors advanced HK$0.05 to HK$1.80.
SEZ Real Estate, aided by institutional buying, firmed HK$0.05 to HK$3.13 on volume of 268,200 shares.

Guangdong Power was the most activlely traded issue, holding steady at HK$5.39 on trade of 662,600 shares. Shenzhen Petrochemical put in the weakest performance on profit-taking, brokers said. The counter slid HK$0.07 to HK$2.42 on thin trade of 13,900 shares.
The A share market advanced in heavy trade on Monday, with speculative buying remaining focused on third-liners, brokers said.
Some funds had been diverted from the stock market in Shanghai, they added.
The A share index climbed 10.33 points, or 3.57 percent, to end at its 1996 high of 300.11, with turnover swelling to 9.10 billion yuan from 6.3 6 billion yuan on Friday.
The composite index rose 9.24 points, or 3.38 percent, to finish at 282.28.
Retailer Shaanxi Minsheng surged 1.86 yuan, or 25.41 percent, to 9.18 yuan.
Shenyang Fangtian soared 1.79 yuan, or 24.55 percent, to 9.08 yuan.
